recipes.name: High-Altitude Challah
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)

steps.text: Dissolve ½ teaspoon sugar and yeast in warm water in a measuring cup. Let stand until the yeast dissolves and starts to foam, 5 to 10 minutes.

Beat 2 eggs in a large bowl. Put egg yolks in a measuring cup; add enough milk to equal ⅓ cup (including yolks). Add yolk mixture to beaten eggs; stir in yeast mixture, butter, salt and remaining 2 tablespoons plus 2 ½ teaspoons sugar. Gradually mix in flour until dough is firm enough to handle.

Turn dough out onto a floured surface; knead until it does not stick to your hands. You will probably use more flour while kneading. Place dough in a large lightly-oiled bowl and turn to coat. Cover and let rise until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.

Cut dough into 3 or 4 even portions; roll into long ropes. Braid ropes and tuck ends under. Place loaf on a baking sheet and cover loosely with plastic wrap. Set in a warm place to rise. Bread is ready to bake when your finger leaves an impression in the dough when pressed.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Whisk remaining 1 egg in a cup with a fork; brush onto loaf. This will give the bread a lovely golden color and delicious crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden and loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom, about 35 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: High-Altitude Challah
raw_recipe.description: This high-altitude challah bread recipe is rich from eggs, butter, and milk. Before baking, sprinkle it with poppy seeds or sesame seeds if you like.

review.reviewBody: Fabulous, reliable, can be made with oil instead of butter for those keeping kosher. I have a sea-level recipe that is not nearly as good...planning to try to adapt this one to sea level this week!

Love this bread, family loves it! Made 4 loaves this weekend, kept one at home, and took 3 to a church potluck. There's not even one slice left. Just a note... I use the leftover egg whites from the separated eggs to brush on the loaf before baking, works great.
Worked well at 6500 ft. At this alt use 25% less yeast. I used the left over egg white to brush on the bread before baking . Will use again.

This recipe uses a ton of eggs compared to other challah recipes, and I love it for that. 45 minutes seems to be the right time for the second rise - one batch I rose for 1 hour 15 minutes and that was too much - it flattened out a little when baking.

We live in New Mexico so we have an obligation to put green chiles in literally everything - I put 7 extra-hot chiles diced right into the dough before kneading and it came out unbelievably delicious and the whole house smelled like chile.
I’m at 8300 feet, I used 3 1/4C of flour, allowed for a smidge more rise time and used one of the egg whites for the wash. I also separated into 6ths for the braid. It is a gorgeous challah loaf.

I am new to the very high altitude baking. We live at almost 9,000ft. I am also new to the world of baking bread. Let me tell you, this was one of the best breads I've ever made. I substituted coconut milk and I also used olive oil instead of butter. This turned out so crispy on the outside and light and fluffy on the inside. I will definitely make it again and next time I might try making a sweet glaze for over the top. My boyfriend compared it to a croissant ??

Absolutely amazing! First rise was 1 hour at room temp, and the second was just about two hours in the fridge (we had to run an errand). Egg wash and baked when we got home for 30 mins and it came out PERFECT! I wish it was a tiny bit sweeter— I think the challahs I used to buy back home in Brooklyn were sweeter— but that may be a preference. THANK YOU for this recipe!

This has an amazing rise and even puffed a bit in the oven while baking. I added a tbsp spoonful of minced garlic, dry garlic not wet, not full of juice, and powdered rosemary I crushed in my mortar and pestle so it had little pieces of rosemary needles. Can't believe this came out in one try! Oh yeah, I am at 6,200 feet altitude.

I have used this recipe for a couple of weeks and it is wonderful! I live in Colorado, so it helps that you live here also! The only thing I change is how much flower I use, I only use 3 cups. When I use an extra half it gets a little to dry.

We live at 5,280 feet, and this recipe worked perfectly for us! It looked gorgeous, too. We followed the directions exactly, except we braided the bread with 5 strands, and we sprinkled sesame seeds on top after the egg wash but before popping it in the oven.
We're at 6K ft and this turned out great. Used olive oil instead of butter, was delish.
Beautiful challah! I’m at @5k and had no problems. I would post a picture but I don’t see anywhere to do that.

I actually just use the bread machine to mix to dough stage. I remove to let it rise of course. I am at about 4k feet in northern Arizona. Turns out great every time, a real winner! Thanks for sharing recipe!

So easy to make! Was testing the recipe for a friend who lives at 6K feet. I live at 3500 ft. Went together easy and tastes delicious! The extra eggs makes a difference. Thank you for sharing your recipe!
Tastes amazing fresh out of the oven. Light but filling. Crust is perfection!
I’m at altitude 6160 and I followed the recipe as written. It’s absolutely delicious!

This bread was excellnt as I also live in Colorado.

 The only thing i did different was i used THC infused Coconut oil. It came out perfect. I saved this recipe & will ise it often. Thanks
Great recipe, and easy. Don't think twice about using 2 packs of yeast. The result is tasty bread with a wonderful yeasty aroma. I live at 3600 feet and this is now my go-to bread recipe.

Works great although I'm not sure it needs that much yeast. I used a mixture of WW flour, AP flour and bread flour. Also, there is enough to make 2 smaller loaves with this too. As this is my first challah, I'm not sure what is good and what isn't. This is overall a good bread for sure.
Delicious! I live at 9500ft, this recipe turned out great! I can't stop eating it. Fast and easy too.
